The main river works for the bridge substructure and temporary support piers are complete and are awaiting the arrival 
of the bridge superstructure from Belgium in April 2025.  Works to the pier protection system are ongoing.   
Image: Bridge substructure: four temporary steel support frames positioned between each of the permanent concrete 
piers, pier protection works to the west of the substructure is ongoing
The fi t-out of the bridge superstructure with the automated mechanical and electrical plant needed for the opening of 
the central bridge spans is progressing in Belgium. The construction of the new public plaza area on the South Quays is 
ongoing and the plant room to operate the bridge from the South Plaza is substantially complete.  
The in-situ reinforced concrete frame and structural steelwork for the roof of the Transport Hub are all complete.  
The installation of the roof decking, internal blockwork and stairs are ongoing.  The southern platform is substantially 
complete except for the area at the western footbridge, where foundations works are progressing for this access bridge.  
The new permanent traffi c lights at the junction of Abbey Road and Fountain 
Street are in operation, but traffi c management continues in operation for 
vehicles and pedestrians to facilitate access arrangements.  The works to 
the inbound footpath and adjacent traffi c lane on Fountain Street are close 
to completion.  Single lane traffi c management continues in operation along 
Dock Road to facilitate adjacent bridge works and to allow for footpath, 
kerbing and ducting along the northern footpath and adjacent traffi c lane. The 
roadworks in Ferrybank will continue in the run up to Christmas, and traffi c will 
continue to be managed and monitored during this period. 
Arrangements to start construction works for the railway fl ood defence and 
drainage works are currently being fi nalised, with works due to commence in 
the new year. These works are designed to make the existing and new rail 
infrastructure climate resilient into the future and protect it from the 
increasing impacts of climate change. The works will include the construction 
of a trackside steel pile fl ood wall, drainage network and pumping stations 
from the Sally Park side, through Plunkett Station car parks and through 
the full extent of the North Quays site and will involve deep pile driving and 
excavations beside the live commuter and freight railway lines. The project is 
liaising with Irish Rail in the management of the construction works to 
maximise effi ciency and minimise impacts on rail lines and services.

2024/2025 OUTDOOR RECREATION INFRASTRUCTURE SCHEME
The Minister for Rural and Community Development, Heather Humphreys TD, launched the 2024/2025 Outdoor 
Recreation Infrastructure Scheme on 17th October last. WCCC will administer the scheme and on 25th October issued 
a call for Expressions of Interest to community groups and Trail Management Organisations in Waterford. This call for 
EOI’s closed on 22nd November. 
EOI’s received are being assessed in line with national criteria and applicants will be informed of the outcome before the 
end of the year. Successful EOIs will then be submitted by WCCC to the DRCD for consideration for funding under the 
ORIS. The deadline for Measure 1 and Project Development Measure is 14th February 2025. The deadline for 
Measures 2 and 3 projects is 28th March 2025.

Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) Draft Annual Revised Map
On the 1st day of February last, Waterford City and County Council prepared and published the RZLT draft annual 
revised map for the 2025 tax liability year. The following stages and timeline apply to the annual mapping process:
1.Publication of a draft annual revised map followed by a 2-month period of public consultation, accompanied by 
placement of advertisements in local press and across Waterford Council social media accounts;
2.Receipt of written submissions from landowners and consideration thereof;
3.Notifi cation of written determinations made by Waterford Council to the relevant landowners who made written 
submissions to the draft map;
4.Making of appeals to An Bord Pleanála where landowners are aggrieved by the determination of the council; and,
5.Publication of fi nal annual revised map at the start of the relevant tax liability year followed by a repeat of the process 
to prepare a new draft annual revised map. 
We are currently in stage 5 in this timeline. A total of two appeals (ref WFD - C30 - 10 and WFD - C30 - 14) have been 
made to An Bord Pleanála relating to our own determinations to retain lands as in-scope for the purposes of the tax. The 
fi nal determinations of An Bord Pleanála have upheld the view of the planning authority, and the relevant lands remain 
in-scope for the tax.  We will now proceed to publish the fi nal annual map for 31st January 2025 and prepare a new 
draft annual revised map for publication on the 1st February 2025.

ACTIVE LAND MANAGEMENT AND DERELICT SITES TEAM
The team is currently addressing a total of 305 properties classified as either derelict or potentially derelict. In recent 
weeks and months, there has been a significant increase in activity, with 102 properties now listed on the Derelict Sites 
Register.  Initial engagement with property owners or their representatives is crucial for resolving dereliction issues and 
gaining insights into the various factors contributing to the properties’ current state.  
                   
The level of activity in the property market concerning vacant and derelict properties has notably increased.  Among the 
properties we have identified as derelict, several have been reintroduced to the private market voluntarily, with some 
currently at the ‘sale agreed’ or ‘to let’ stages.  We are actively engaging with the new owners of these properties to 
ensure they are fully informed of their obligations under the Derelict Sites Act 1990.  Additionally, the introduction of the 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has contributed to a significant rise in the number of derelict and vacant 
properties available on the market at this time.

Community Recognition Fund (CRF)– Window 2 and Window 3
Window 2
We have yet to receive final approval from the Department of Rural and Community Development for the two projects 
recommended for funding under Window 2 of the Community Recognition Fund 2024, which we anticipate should be 
within the coming weeks.  
Window 3 of this fund is due to launch on the 4th December 2024, with a deadline for receipt of applications by 4.00pm 
on the 8th January 2025. 
The minimum level of funding for a project is €50,000 and is targeted at, and specifically invested in those communities, 
villages and towns where the highest level of new arrivals is located and where there is a clear need for investment 
identified. Projects need to be capital in nature and must address needs in their areas and deliver medium-long term 
benefits for the entire community and be capable of being delivered over the course of 2025 and 2026 (up to 30th

THE CONTROL OF DOGS (XL BULLY TYPE DOG) REGULATIONS 2024
The Control of Dogs (XL Bully Type Dog) Regulations 2024 prohibit the importing, breeding, selling and re-homing of XL 
Bully type dogs from 1st October 2024.  From 1st February 2025 it will be illegal to own an XL Bully type dog without a 
‘Certificate of Exemption’ issued by the local authority in which the dog resides.
XL Bully owners have between 1st October 2024 and 31st January 2025 to apply for a Certificate of Exemption.  A 
Certificate of Exemption is issued by the Local Authority and authorises the owner of an XL Bully type dog to keep that dog 
at a particular premises until the natural end of the dog’s life.
This certificate is unique to each XL Bully type dog and owner, and specifies the dog’s licence details, microchip details, 
neutering details, age and description. It also specifies the dog owner’s name, address, date of birth and contact number. 
To date the Dog Control Unit has received three valid applications for a Certificate of Exemption.  Two of these 
applications have been approved and issued with a Certificate of Exemption.  The third application is on hold pending 
further information.  
After 1st February 2025 all XL Bully type dog owners should either be in possession of a Certificate of Exemption or have 
proof that they applied for a Certificate of Exemption.  Owners may be required to present their Certificate of Exemption 
to a Dog Warden or a member of An Garda Síochána within 10 Days of a request to do so.
Owners can apply, free of charge, to Waterford City & County Council from 1st October 2024 for a Certificate of Exemption 
through our website, through email or by post.   Further details are available on our website or at www.gov.ie/xlbully
